sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a two-arm trial; the probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\) are known protocol-fixed design inputs and are not conditions defining either compatible-law class.
sampling_model.units: Each unit has finite genomic profile \(Z\), a predeclared continuous score \(R\), bounded potential event times, and potential censoring times.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) is independent of \((T(0),T(1),C(0),C(1))\) conditional on \(X=(Z,R)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The lower bounds \(\pi_a(x)\ge\varepsilon\) hold for both treatment arms, and uncensored probability is bounded below by \(\kappa\). Because treatment is binary and the two allocation probabilities sum to one, \(\pi_a(x)\le1-\varepsilon\) is a consequence rather than a separate overlap restriction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The bounded score-density and known-\(\beta\) Hölder conditions are explicit maintained regularity restrictions. No nuisance-band theorem is inferred from them. Inference is stated only over the externally certified subclass \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\), with abstract radius \(r_n\), and the empirical-process prerequisite is imposed only on \(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\).

tldr: Informative dropout leaves an unknown residual restricted-survival contribution along the predeclared prognostic score. The greatest feasible monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz residual below a capacity \(u\) is the explicit envelope \(\Gamma_Lu\), which gives the exact pointwise projection of the law-sharp compact CATE-curve set. Joint curve coupling is nontrivial: the maintained set is strictly smaller than the Wang endpoint-selection box exactly when some arm-profile dropout capacity is nonzero. Support values separate into certified path-flow obstacle programs, and eroded grids have a uniform Hausdorff remainder even at zero-capacity contacts. For inference, a direct positive-part stability argument turns an externally certified nuisance band into an observable clipped compact convex whole-set superset with directed excess \(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), without face differentiation or a direction net. Combining the density band with a finite-multinomial profile-mass region gives conservative simultaneous intervals for every eligible leaf and arbitrary post-selection validity. Efficient local-mass \((np_{\min,n})^{-1/2}\) calibration remains open because the declared score assumptions contain no score-to-statistic expansion or multiplier coupling.

project_justification.gap: Wang et al. prove covariatewise outer endpoint validity under their treatment-exchangeability, overlap, and consistency conditions, but do not characterize the jointly attainable curve image, its exact contraction under score-shape restrictions, or an estimated-obstacle confidence set that remains valid when capacity contacts change. Generic support-function and directional-bootstrap results do not supply the missing score-to-statistic expansion for the present obstacle program.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is simultaneously causal and functional: a law-sharp compact set of whole CATE curves, an exact published-class benchmark modulo \(P_X\)-null sets, a finite flow certificate, and an observable confidence superset whose validity does not depend on stable active faces.
project_justification.fill: Completion witnesses establish exact population identification in the monotone-Lipschitz class and transfer converse attainability from the continuous witness subclass to the full Wang-compatible class. The envelope, strictness, support-flow, grid-Hausdorff, and stability results characterize and compute the population set. On the externally certified band-valid subclass, the proved band-robust theorem establishes uniform containment of the true curve set in the robust union together with shrinking directed excess; a finite-multinomial baseline-law region yields conservative simultaneous leaf projections with the theorem's stated outer-probability guarantee. Only the sharper derivative-aware local-mass multiplier rate is left unresolved.

related_work: Wang et al. (2025, Assumption 3.1, Theorem 5.1, equations (8)--(9), and Appendix D.2) provide treatment-exchangeability, overlap, consistency, and conservative arm and CATE endpoint results. This note first states their compatible-law class explicitly, proves their endpoint-selection box is the full measurable image modulo \(P_X\)-null sets by transferring completion witnesses from a smaller continuous subclass, and then shows that its continuous slice is \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). The maintained monotone-Lipschitz model is a distinct sensitivity class: its greatest-obstacle envelope gives exact pointwise projections, and its joint curve image is strictly smaller than the Wang box if and only if at least one capacity is nonzero. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari inform the support-function view of set identification; Kim informs primal--dual certification; and Chiang et al. inform finite linear encodings of shape restrictions. None supplies the informative-dropout completion or the exact obstacle envelope proved here. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker, Fang and Santos, and Semenova motivate derivative-aware inference for optimized maps, but their results do not create a score-to-statistic expansion for an estimated infinite-dimensional obstacle with changing contacts. The present whole-set theorem instead uses a direct Hausdorff contraction and an external nuisance band, so it needs neither face differentiation nor a direction net. Wei et al. motivate simultaneous subgroup inference for a supplied family of point-identified effects; here density-band and finite-multinomial uncertainty are propagated through a partially identified curve set to give conservative simultaneous and post-selection leaf intervals. The efficient local-mass multiplier refinement remains a separate open problem.
technical_internal_limitation: The completion uses the convention \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{C\le T\}\), so assigning \(T=C\) to the non-maximal branch remains recorded as dropout. If a data system codes ties as observed events, exact attainment at zero residual may fail and the sharp object can become a closure; that alternative convention must be audited before application.
honest_scope: Population claims are exact but class-specific. The maintained monotone-Lipschitz compatible-law class has the law-sharp curve set and exact \(\Gamma_Lu\) pointwise projection; the full Wang-compatible class has the measurable endpoint-selection box modulo \(P_X\)-null sets, with \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) as its continuous slice. The finite-\(L\) and monotonicity restrictions are novel identifying sensitivities, while score density and known-\(\beta\) Hölder regularity are explicit regularity conditions. No nuisance band is derived from those conditions: inference is uniform only over the externally certified subclass. On the band event, the proved whole-set superset covers and has directed excess at most \(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), uniformly through changing contacts. Conservative leaf intervals additionally use a finite-multinomial profile-mass region; their displayed excess shrinks under \((r_n+n^{-1/2})/p_{\min,n}\to0\), which is stronger than the desired local-mass regime. The current envelope, moment, and entropy assumptions do not imply a statistic expansion or conditional multiplier approximation, so no efficient \((np_{\min,n})^{-1/2}\) leaf claim is made. Post-selection validity is deterministic on the simultaneous event. An ADJUVANT sign reanalysis still requires individual trial records, a genuinely predeclared score, eligible leaf mass, and a defensible sensitivity value \(L\); absent those inputs, no empirical subgroup sign is asserted.

novel.justification: This maintained full-design condition is satisfied by trials that draw treatment from the known allocation rule using baseline \(X\) before either potential event or potential censoring time is realized. Complete, block, and stratified randomization based only on \(X\) are concrete admissible designs.

This explicit regularity condition requires the prespecified score to retain observations throughout its normalized range within every genomic profile. It can be checked before outcome analysis by profile-specific score histograms and density bands; profiles with sparse boundary support are coarsened or the analysis is restricted to a prespecified common-support interval.

assumptions.condition: \(\max_{a\in\mathcal A,\,z\in\mathcal Z}\{\|b_{a,z}\|_{\mathcal H^\beta},\|u_{a,z}\|_{\mathcal H^\beta}\}\vee\max_{z\in\mathcal Z}\|p_z\|_{\mathcal H^\beta}\le M\).

novel.justification: This explicit regularity condition is plausible for a continuously scaled prognostic score when conditional follow-up, dropout capacity, and score density have no abrupt clinical threshold. The exponent \(\beta\in(0,1]\) is treated as known and fixed before inference, chosen from prespecified smoothness classes supported by external or pilot-only diagnostics; sensitivity is reported over a small prespecified set of candidate exponents.

This mild continuity-only benchmark rules out jumps in mean hidden restricted-survival time along a continuously scaled predeclared prognosis score, without imposing a direction or a finite slope bound. It is assessed by varying score binning in an external near-complete-follow-up cohort and is used only to define the continuous-function comparator class.

assumptions.condition: With \(R\) oriented before analysis so that larger scores indicate weakly longer event-free prognosis, \(s_{a,z}(r)\le s_{a,z}(r')\quad\forall a\in\mathcal A,\ z\in\mathcal Z,\ 0\le r\le r'\le1\).

novel.justification: This identifying restriction says that, within a genomic profile and treatment arm, patients with a better predeclared prognosis cannot have a smaller mean amount of event-free time hidden by dropout. Its orientation is fixed without using outcomes. A validation and sensitivity protocol compares monotone trends of completed-minus-observed restricted survival in an external near-complete-follow-up cohort, then reports the identified set both with this sign restriction and with monotonicity removed.

assumptions.condition: \(|s_{a,z}(r)-s_{a,z}(r')|\le L|r-r'|\quad\forall a\in\mathcal A,\ z\in\mathcal Z,\ r,r'\in[0,1]\).

novel.justification: This identifying sensitivity restriction caps how quickly hidden event-free time can change along the prespecified score. Clinicians can elicit a maximum change \(d\) in hidden restricted-survival time over a score increment \(\delta_r\), set \(L=d/\delta_r\), compare that calibration with an external near-complete-follow-up cohort, and report a curve of conclusions over a prespecified grid of \(L\), including the residual-continuity-only benchmark.

This is an external high-level band prerequisite, not a consequence of the randomized-design model or the stated Hölder restriction. It is operational when an independent calibration sample, a pilot-only procedure, or a separately proved honest-band method certifies the displayed property; all inferential claims are restricted to the certified subclass.

Vanishing of the abstract external band radius is imposed only on the band-valid triangular-array subclass. It is plausible when the prespecified score is one-dimensional and an external or pilot-only band construction is available, but it is not asserted to follow from the maintained law class.

definitions.name: Observed base function
definitions.construction: \(b_{a,z}(r)=E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[\widetilde T\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\).

definitions.name: Dropout capacity
definitions.construction: \(u_{a,z}(r)=E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\).

definitions.name: Residual contribution
definitions.construction: \(s_{a,z}^{P}(r)=E_{P}[(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\).

definitions.name: Model class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P=\{P:\ P\text{ is a full-data law satisfying each listed causal, support, overlap, observed-law regularity, and residual-shape property}\}\).

definitions.name: Observed-law-compatible full-data class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{P\in\mathfrak P:\mathcal L_P(Z,R,A,\min\{T(A),C(A)\},\mathbf 1\{C(A)\le T(A)\})=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).

definitions.name: Residual-continuity-only model class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cont}}=\{P:\ P\text{ is a full-data law satisfying the listed causal, support, overlap, observed-law regularity, and residual-continuity properties, with no monotonicity or finite Lipschitz restriction}\}\).

definitions.name: Residual-continuity-only compatible-law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{P\in\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{cont}}:\mathcal L_P(Z,R,A,\min\{T(A),C(A)\},\mathbf 1\{C(A)\le T(A)\})=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).

definitions.name: Arm-profile obstacle set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{f\in C([0,1]):0\le f(r)\le u_{a,z}(r),\ f(r)\le f(r')\text{ for }r\le r',\ |f(r)-f(r')|\le L|r-r'|\text{ for all }r,r'\in[0,1]\}\).

definitions.name: Flow-sharp CATE-curve set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}:f_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\text{ for every }a,z\}\subset\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\).

definitions.name: Residual-continuity-only CATE image
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{g\in\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}:g_z(r)\in[b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-u_{0,z}(r),\ b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+u_{1,z}(r)]\ \forall(z,r)\in\mathcal Z\times[0,1]\}\).

definitions.name: Armwise completion witness
definitions.construction: For \(f_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), set \(q_{a,z}(r)=f_{a,z}(r)/u_{a,z}(r)\) on \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\) and \(q_{a,z}(r)=0\) on \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\). Conditional on \(X=(z,r)\), draw \((\widetilde T_a,\Delta_a)\) independently across arms from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}((\widetilde T,\Delta)\in\cdot\mid A=a,X=(z,r))\). If \(\Delta_a=0\), set \(T(a)=\widetilde T_a\) and \(C(a)=t_{\max}+1\). If \(\Delta_a=1\), set \(C(a)=\widetilde T_a\) and set \(T(a)=t_{\max}\) with probability \(q_{a,z}(r)\), otherwise \(T(a)=\widetilde T_a\). Finally draw \(A\) independently given \(X\) with probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\); the resulting law is \(P^f\).

definitions.name: Residual-continuity-only box completion
definitions.construction: For \(g\in\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), set \(f^g_{1,z}(r)=[g_z(r)-b_{1,z}(r)+b_{0,z}(r)]_+\) and \(f^g_{0,z}(r)=[-g_z(r)+b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)]_+\), and set \(q^g_{a,z}=f^g_{a,z}/u_{a,z}\) on \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\) and zero on \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\). Conditional on \(X=(z,r)\), draw \((\widetilde T_a,\Delta_a)\) independently across arms from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}((\widetilde T,\Delta)\in\cdot\mid A=a,X=(z,r))\). If \(\Delta_a=0\), set \(T(a)=\widetilde T_a\) and \(C(a)=t_{\max}+1\). If \(\Delta_a=1\), set \(C(a)=\widetilde T_a\) and set \(T(a)=t_{\max}\) with probability \(q^g_{a,z}(r)\), otherwise \(T(a)=\widetilde T_a\). Draw \(A\) independently given \(X\) with the protocol-fixed probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\); the resulting law is \(P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}\).

definitions.name: Continuous support and obstacle values
definitions.construction: \(h_{\mathcal T}(v)=\sup_{g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})}\sum_z\int g_z(r)\,dv_z(r)\) and \(V_{a,z}(w;u)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})}\int f(r)\,dw(r)\).

definitions.name: Piecewise-linear interpolation
definitions.construction: \(\Phi_h x=\sum_{j=0}^{m}x_j\phi_{j,h}\), where \(\phi_{j,h}\) is the standard hat basis on \(r_j=jh\).

definitions.name: Eroded gridded obstacle
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal S^h_{a,z}=\{\Phi_hx:0\le x_j\le[u_{a,z}(r_j)-Mh^\beta]_+,\ 0\le x_{j+1}-x_j\le Lh,\ j=0,\ldots,m-1\}\).

definitions.name: Path-transshipment dual
definitions.construction: Let \(\bar u_j=[u_{a,z}(r_j)-Mh^\beta]_+\). Define \(\mathcal D_h(w,\bar u)\) as all nonnegative \(d_h=(\lambda^+,\lambda^-,g,d)\) with \(\lambda_j^+,\lambda_j^-\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m\) and \(g_j,d_j\) for \(j=0,\ldots,m-1\) satisfying \(\lambda_j^+-\lambda_j^-+g_{j-1}-g_j+d_j-d_{j-1}=w_j\), with \(g_{-1}=g_m=d_{-1}=d_m=0\). Its cost is \(\sum_{j=0}^{m}\bar u_j\lambda_j^+ +Lh\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}g_j\).

definitions.name: Gridded curve set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_h(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f^h_{1,z}-f^h_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}:f^h_{a,z}\in\mathcal S^h_{a,z}\text{ for every }a,z\}\).

definitions.name: Eligible genomic leaves
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_n=\{G\in\mathcal G:P_X(G)\ge p_{\min,n}\}\).

definitions.name: Leaf benefit and its identified interval
definitions.construction: \(\ell_G(g;Q)=Q(G)^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\int\mathbf 1\{(z,r)\in G\}g_z(r)\,dQ(z,r)\), and \([\underline\theta_G,\overline\theta_G]=[\inf_{g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})}\ell_G(g;P_X),\sup_{g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})}\ell_G(g;P_X)]\).

definitions.name: Changing-contact inference handle
definitions.construction: Critical-cone obstacle handle: starting from the externally supplied band \(\widehat{\mathcal B}_{\eta,n}\), restrict support calibration to the finite net \(\mathcal D_n\), and at mesh \(h_n\) construct the radius-\(\mathsf R\)-clipped set \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_{n,h_n}^{+}\), \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{X,n}\), and all \(\widehat I_G\) by a robust obstacle program that re-solves the active contact face, a Fang--Santos estimated directional derivative, and one common multiplier supremum over \(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\).

definitions.name: Projected conservative simultaneous leaf intervals
definitions.construction:
For every \(G\in\mathcal G\), let
\[
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{G,n}
=\left\{(g,Q):g\in\widehat{\mathcal T}_{n,h_n}^{+},\
Q\in\widehat{\mathcal P}_{X,n},\ Q(G)\geq p_{\min,n}/2\right\}.
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{G,n}\neq\varnothing\), define
\[
\widehat I_G=
\left[
\inf_{(g,Q)\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{G,n}}\ell_G(g;Q),
\ \sup_{(g,Q)\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{G,n}}\ell_G(g;Q)
\right].
\]
If \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{G,n}=\varnothing\), define the observable fallback \(\widehat I_G=[-\mathsf R,\mathsf R]\).  Intervals are therefore constructed for the entire predeclared class; the theorem supplies simultaneous guarantees for every mass-eligible \(G\in\mathcal G_n\).

definitions.name: Externally band-valid subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)=\{P\in\mathfrak P:\operatorname{Cert}_n(P;r_n)=1\}\).

definitions.name: External-band-calibrated analysis mesh
definitions.construction: \(h_n=\left\lceil\max\{1,((L+M)/r_n)^{1/\beta}\}\right\rceil^{-1}\), so \(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta=O(r_n)\).

definitions.name: Finite support-direction net
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D_n\) is any finite \(\delta_n\)-net, in the dual norm, of \(\{v\in(\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z,h_n})^*:\|v\|_*\le1\}\); finiteness follows because \(\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z,h_n}\) is finite dimensional.

definitions.name: Greatest-obstacle envelope
definitions.construction:
For every arm \(a\in\mathcal A\), profile \(z\in\mathcal Z\), and score \(r\in[0,1]\), define
\[
(\Gamma_Lu_{a,z})(r)
:=\inf_{t\in[0,1]}\{u_{a,z}(t)+L(r-t)_+\},
\qquad (x)_+:=\max\{x,0\}.
\]

definitions.name: Wang-compatible full-data class
definitions.construction: The Wang-compatible class \(\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) consists of full-data laws satisfying Wang Assumption 3.1: the displayed event-time consistency condition, pointwise treatment overlap, treatment exchangeability \(T(a)\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\), and pointwise censoring overlap, while inducing the observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and obeying \(0\le T(a)\le t_{\max}\). No continuity, monotonicity, finite-Lipschitz, or independent-censoring restriction is imposed. The completion proof uses laws with a full potential-censoring representation as a smaller witness subclass; converse attainment by that subclass transfers upward to the published Wang class.

definitions.name: Wang measurable endpoint-selection box
definitions.construction:
Let \(L^0(P_X)\) denote equivalence classes, modulo \(P_X\)-null sets, of measurable profile-score functions.  Define
\[
\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
:=\left\{g\in L^0(P_X):
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-u_{0,z}(r)
\leq g_z(r)\leq
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+u_{1,z}(r)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}\right\}.
\]

definitions.name: Band-robust contact-stable confidence construction (outer-probability version)
definitions.construction:
Put
\[
\widehat\gamma_z=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{Z_i=z\},
\qquad
\varepsilon_{Z,n}=2\sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal Z|}{n\alpha}},
\qquad
e_{h_n}=2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta).
\]
Let \(\widehat{\mathcal E}_n\) be the set of triples \((b',u',p')\in\widehat{\mathcal B}_{\eta,n}\) such that, for every arm and profile, \(u'_{a,z}\geq0\), \(p'_z\geq0\), \(\int_0^1p'_z(r)\,dr=1\), \(c_p\leq p'_z\leq C_p\), and
\[
\max_{a,z}\{\|b'_{a,z}\|_{\mathcal H^\beta},\|u'_{a,z}\|_{\mathcal H^\beta}\}
\vee\max_z\|p'_z\|_{\mathcal H^\beta}\leq M.
\]
Define the finite-multinomial region
\[
\widehat\Gamma_n=
\left\{\gamma\in[0,1]^{|\mathcal Z|}:\sum_z\gamma_z=1,
\ \sum_z|\gamma_z-\widehat\gamma_z|\leq\varepsilon_{Z,n}\right\}
\]
and the preliminary baseline-law region
\[
\widehat{\mathcal P}^{\,0}_{X,n}
=\left\{Q:Q(\{z\}\times dr)=\gamma_zp'_z(r)\,dr
\text{ for some }(b',u',p')\in\widehat{\mathcal E}_n,
\ \gamma\in\widehat\Gamma_n\right\}.
\]
Set \(\widehat{\mathcal P}_{X,n}=\widehat{\mathcal P}^{\,0}_{X,n}\) when this set is nonempty, and otherwise use the observable fallback singleton containing \(Q^0(\{z\}\times dr)=|\mathcal Z|^{-1}dr\).

Let
\[
\mathcal K_{\mathsf R,M,L,\beta}
=\left\{g\in\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}:\|g\|_\infty\leq\mathsf R,
\ |g_z(r)-g_z(r')|
\leq2M|r-r'|^\beta+2L|r-r'|\ \forall z,r,r'\right\}.
\]
For \((b',u',p')\in\widehat{\mathcal E}_n\), let \(\mathcal T_{h_n}(b',u')\) denote the gridded-curve construction evaluated at \((b',u')\).  Define
\[
\widehat H_n=
\overline{\operatorname{co}}\!\left(
\bigcup_{(b',u',p')\in\widehat{\mathcal E}_n}
\left\{g+e:g\in\mathcal T_{h_n}(b',u'),\ e\in\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z},\
\|e\|_\infty\leq e_{h_n}\right\}\right)
\cap\mathcal K_{\mathsf R,M,L,\beta}.
\]
The band-robust whole-set confidence set is \(\widehat{\mathcal T}_{n,h_n}^{+}=\widehat H_n\) when \(\widehat H_n\neq\varnothing\), and is the fallback singleton \(\{0\}\) otherwise.  The construction is a sample-indexed set-valued object; all coverage claims below are understood in outer probability, avoiding an undeclared measurable-maximum claim for the uncountable band union. Its ingredients use only the observed sample, the externally supplied nuisance band, and predeclared constants; it does not differentiate or hold fixed an obstacle contact face.

statements.statement: For every family \(f=(f_{a,z})\) with \(f_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the constructed law \(P^f\) belongs to \(\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), has residual contribution \(s_{a,z}^{P^f}=f_{a,z}\), and preserves the observed censoring law. On \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\), attainability follows from \(E[(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid a,z,r]=q_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)=f_{a,z}(r)\); on \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\), feasibility forces \(f_{a,z}=0\), and the tie convention keeps the completion legal.
statements.justification: This is the attainability step that turns valid inequalities into law sharpness, including zero-capacity contacts.
statements.gap: Wang et al. prove endpoint validity in Theorem 5.1 and Appendix D.2 but do not construct one full-data completion attaining an entire shape-coupled curve.
statements.consumer: It lets trial analysts interpret every reported curve in the set as arising from an observationally equivalent informative-dropout law.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a feasible family \(f=(f_{a,z})\).  By the obstacle-set definition,
\[
0\leq f_{a,z}(r)\leq u_{a,z}(r)\qquad(a\in\mathcal A,\ z\in\mathcal Z,\ r\in[0,1]).
\]
Consequently the completion probability in the armwise completion definition is well defined and satisfies
\[
q_{a,z}(r)=\frac{f_{a,z}(r)}{u_{a,z}(r)}\in[0,1]
\quad\hbox{if }u_{a,z}(r)>0.
\]
If \(u_{a,z}(r)=0\), the same obstacle inequality forces \(f_{a,z}(r)=0\), and the stipulated value \(q_{a,z}(r)=0\) again gives
\[
q_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)=f_{a,z}(r).                                      \qquad\text{(1)}
\]
The piecewise ratio is Borel measurable because \(f_{a,z}\) and \(u_{a,z}\) are continuous and \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\) is open.

We next verify the observation map event by event.  Write \((\widetilde T_a,\Delta_a)\) for the arm-\(a\) draw in the construction.  When \(\Delta_a=0\), the construction gives
\[
T(a)=\widetilde T_a\leq t_{\max}<t_{\max}+1=C(a),
\]
so
\[
\min\{T(a),C(a)\}=\widetilde T_a,
\qquad \mathbf 1\{C(a)\leq T(a)\}=0=\Delta_a.                         \qquad\text{(2)}
\]
When \(\Delta_a=1\), it gives \(C(a)=\widetilde T_a\) and \(T(a)\in\{\widetilde T_a,t_{\max}\}\).  Since \(0\leq\widetilde T_a\leq t_{\max}\),
\[
\min\{T(a),C(a)\}=\widetilde T_a,
\qquad \mathbf 1\{C(a)\leq T(a)\}=1=\Delta_a.                         \qquad\text{(3)}
\]
The weak inequality in (3) is precisely where the stipulated tie-as-dropout convention is used.  Equations (2)--(3), the observed marginal law of \(X\) used by the completion, the observed conditional kernel of \((\widetilde T_a,\Delta_a)\) given \(A=a,X\), and the protocol probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\) show that the observation map under \(P^f\) has law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  In particular, the law of the observed censoring record \((\widetilde T,\Delta)\), conditionally and marginally, is preserved.

The Bernoulli completion coin is conditionally independent of \((\widetilde T_a,\Delta_a)\) given \(X=(z,r)\), and its success probability is \(q_{a,z}(r)\).  Treatment is drawn only after the two potential arm records and independently of them given \(X\).  Therefore, using randomization and the dropout-capacity definition,
\[
\begin{aligned}
&E_{P^f}[(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&\quad=q_{a,z}(r)
E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta
 \mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&\quad=q_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)
=f_{a,z}(r),                                                            \qquad\text{(4)}
\end{aligned}
\]
where the final equality includes both the positive-capacity and zero-capacity cases by (1).  Thus the residual-contribution definition gives \(s^{P^f}_{a,z}=f_{a,z}\).

It remains to check membership rather than merely observational equivalence.  Defining realized \((T,C)=(T(A),C(A))\) gives consistency.  Drawing \(A\) independently of all potential arm records conditional on \(X\) gives the stated randomization property.  Equations (2)--(3) and the support of the observed record give \(0\leq T(a)\leq t_{\max}\).  All treatment-overlap, censoring-overlap, profile-mass, score-density, and observed-law H\"older conditions are inherited from the unchanged observed law.  Finally, (4) identifies the residual functions with \(f_{a,z}\), which are nonnegative, nondecreasing, and \(L\)-Lipschitz by feasibility.  These are exactly the membership conditions in the compatible-law definition.  Hence \(P^f\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), with the claimed residual contribution and preserved observed censoring law.

statements.statement: The identified set of profile-specific CATE curves is exactly \(\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}=\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). The set \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) is nonempty, compact, and convex in \(\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\).
statements.justification: The theorem replaces unrelated pointwise intervals by the joint law-sharp function-valued causal object.
statements.gap: Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari characterize random-set expectations abstractly, while Wang et al. give only covariatewise survival-CATE endpoints; neither identifies this dropout obstacle image.
statements.consumer: The sharp compact set is the target needed for honest sign statements along a prognostic score and across genomic profiles.
statements.proof_tex:
Define the causal identified set independently of the observed-law functional by
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
:=\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
\subset\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}.
\tag{1}
\]
Fix \(P\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  On \(\{A=a\}\), consistency and the observation definitions imply
\[
T(a)=\widetilde T+(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(\Delta=0\), then \(C(a)>T(a)\) and \(\widetilde T=T(a)\); if \(\Delta=1\), (2) is tautological.  Conditional randomization and treatment overlap give
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_P[T(a)\mid Z=z,R=r]
&=E_P[T(a)\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&=b_{a,z}(r)+s^P_{a,z}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]
The second equality uses (2), compatibility, and the definitions of \(b\) and \(s\).  Subtracting arms yields
\[
\tau_z^P(r)
=b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+s^P_{1,z}(r)-s^P_{0,z}(r).
\tag{4}
\]
Bounded event time gives
\[
0\leq(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta
\leq(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta.
\tag{5}
\]
Taking conditional expectations gives
\[
0\leq s^P_{a,z}(r)\leq u_{a,z}(r)
\tag{6}
\]
for the conditional score law almost every \(r\).  The model restrictions make \(s^P_{a,z}\) \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(u_{a,z}\) H\"older continuous.  Profile mass makes the arm-profile conditional law well defined; Bayes' rule, treatment overlap, and the density bound give
\[
\frac{dP_{\mathrm{obs}}(R\in dr\mid A=a,Z=z)}{dr}
=\frac{\pi_a(z,r)p_z(r)}
{P_{\mathrm{obs}}(A=a\mid Z=z)}
\geq\varepsilon c_p>0.
\tag{7}
\]
The denominator is positive and at most one.  A pointwise violation of (6) would persist on a relative interval by continuity, contradicting (7) and almost-sure validity.  Thus (6) holds everywhere.  Residual monotonicity and residual Lipschitz continuity yield
\[
s^P_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\qquad\text{for every }a,z.
\tag{8}
\]
Equations (4) and (8) prove
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{9}
\]

Conversely, take
\[
g=(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}
\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]
The established completion-witness lemma supplies one \(P^f\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) satisfying \(s^{P^f}_{a,z}=f_{a,z}\) simultaneously.  Equation (4) gives \(\tau^{P^f}=g\), so
\[
\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{10}
\]
This proves equality and law sharpness.

For geometry, the zero function belongs to every obstacle set.  Its interval, monotonicity, and Lipschitz inequalities are preserved by convex combinations and uniform limits, so each obstacle set is nonempty, convex, and closed.  Every member obeys
\[
\|f\|_\infty\leq\|u_{a,z}\|_\infty,\qquad
|f(r)-f(r')|\leq L|r-r'|.
\tag{11}
\]
For completeness, take any sequence in one obstacle set, extract a diagonal subsequence converging on a countable dense set, and choose, for each \(\epsilon>0\), a finite dense-set net of mesh below \(\epsilon/(3L)\).  Convergence at its finitely many points and (11) imply, for sufficiently large \(k,\ell\),
\[
\sup_{r\in[0,1]}|f_k(r)-f_\ell(r)|
\leq2L\frac{\epsilon}{3L}+\frac{\epsilon}{3}
=\epsilon.
\tag{12}
\]
The subsequence is uniformly Cauchy, has a continuous uniform limit, and closedness puts that limit in the obstacle set.  Thus the obstacle set is compact in the metric sup-norm topology.

There are \(2|\mathcal Z|\) obstacle factors, so their product is nonempty, compact, and convex.  The affine map
\[
(f_{a,z})_{a,z}\longmapsto
(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}
\tag{13}
\]
is continuous, because the image distance is at most twice the largest coordinatewise input distance.  Its image is \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Continuous affine images preserve nonemptiness, compactness, and convexity, completing the proof.

statements.statement: For every \(v\in\mathbb B_*\), \(h_{\mathcal T}(v)=\sum_z\int(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z})\,dv_z+\sum_z\{V_{1,z}(v_z;u)+V_{0,z}(-v_z;u)\}\). For the grid problem, writing \(w_j=\int\phi_{j,h}\,dv_z\) and \(\bar u_j=[u_{a,z}(r_j)-Mh^\beta]_+\), strong duality gives \(\sup_{x:0\le x_j\le\bar u_j,\,0\le x_{j+1}-x_j\le Lh}\sum_jw_jx_j=\min_{d_h=(\lambda^+,\lambda^-,g,d)\in\mathcal D_h(w,\bar u)}\{\sum_j\bar u_j\lambda_j^+ +Lh\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}g_j\}\). The primal and dual are a path min-cost transshipment pair, and their equality is a finite certificate for each support direction.
statements.justification: A directionwise support identity and primal-dual flow certificate make the infinite-dimensional set auditable rather than merely definitional.
statements.gap: Kim's Theorem 1 uses transport duality for fixed-marginal DTE bounds, and Chiang et al.'s Theorem 1 projects a sieve confidence region by generic linear programs; neither yields the dropout-capacity path dual.
statements.consumer: Software can return a primal curve and a dual certificate for every clinical leaf or plotted support direction.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(v\in\mathbb B_*\).  All the integrals below are finite: each
\(v_z\) has finite total variation, while the functions \(b_{a,z}\) and
every member of \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) are continuous on
the compact interval \([0,1]\).  By the definitions of the sharp curve
set and its support function,
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_{\mathcal T}(v)
&=\sup_{\substack{f_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\\
                   a\in\{0,1\},\ z\in\mathcal Z}}
 \sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\int
 \{b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z}\}\,dv_z \\
&=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}\int(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z})\,dv_z
  +\sup_{(f_{a,z})}\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}
       \left\{\int f_{1,z}\,dv_z+\int f_{0,z}\,d(-v_z)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The feasible family is a finite Cartesian product of nonempty sets, because
the zero function belongs to every obstacle set.  Consequently the last
supremum is the sum of the coordinatewise suprema: the inequality from left
to right is immediate, and the reverse inequality follows by choosing, for
each of the finitely many coordinates, a feasible function within
\(\epsilon/(2|\mathcal Z|)\) of its supremum and then sending
\(\epsilon\downarrow0\).  The definition of \(V_{a,z}\) therefore gives
\[
h_{\mathcal T}(v)
=\sum_z\int(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z})\,dv_z
 +\sum_z\{V_{1,z}(v_z;u)+V_{0,z}(-v_z;u)\}.
\]
This proves the continuous support decomposition.

Fix now one arm-profile pair \((a,z)\), put
\(w_j=\int\phi_{j,h}\,dv_z\), and put
\(\bar u_j=[u_{a,z}(r_j)-Mh^\beta]_+\).  Linearity of integration and the
definition of \(\Phi_h\) yield
\[
 \int\Phi_hx\,dv_z=\sum_{j=0}^m w_jx_j.
\]
Thus the grid support problem is the finite linear program
\[
 p^*=\max_x\left\{\sum_{j=0}^m w_jx_j:
 0\le x_j\le\bar u_j,\quad
 0\le x_{j+1}-x_j\le Lh\ (0\le j<m)\right\}.
\]
Its feasible polytope is nonempty, since it contains \(x=0\), and compact,
since \(0\le x_j\le\bar u_j<\infty\).  Hence it has a maximizer \(x^*\).

For completeness, we derive the specialized dual equality.  Write the four
families of inequalities as
\[
 x_j-\bar u_j\le0,\qquad -x_j\le0,\qquad
 x_{j+1}-x_j-Lh\le0,\qquad x_j-x_{j+1}\le0.
\]
At \(x^*\), the vector \(w=(w_0,\ldots,w_m)\) is a nonnegative linear
combination of the normals of the active inequalities.  Indeed, if it were
not, finite-dimensional separation from the finitely generated cone of
active normals would give a vector \(y\) whose inner product with every
active normal is nonpositive but with \(w^Ty>0\).  Every inactive inequality
has strictly positive slack, so \(x^*+ty\) would remain feasible for all
sufficiently small \(t>0\), contradicting
\(w^T(x^*+ty)>w^Tx^*\).  Denote the resulting nonnegative coefficients by
\(\lambda_j^+,\lambda_j^-,g_j,d_j\), in the order displayed above, and
extend the arc variables by
\(g_{-1}=g_m=d_{-1}=d_m=0\).  Equating the coefficient of \(x_j\) gives
\[
 \lambda_j^+-\lambda_j^-+g_{j-1}-g_j+d_j-d_{j-1}=w_j,
 \qquad j=0,\ldots,m.
\]
Hence \(d_h=(\lambda^+,\lambda^-,g,d)\) belongs to
\(\mathcal D_h(w,\bar u)\).  Because a multiplier can be positive only for
an active constraint,
\[
\begin{aligned}
p^*=w^Tx^*
 &=\sum_{j=0}^m\bar u_j\lambda_j^+
   +Lh\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}g_j.
\end{aligned}
\]
Conversely, for every primal-feasible \(x\) and every
\(d_h\in\mathcal D_h(w,\bar u)\), the balance equations imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_jw_jx_j
&=\sum_j(\lambda_j^+-\lambda_j^-)x_j
 +\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}g_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)
 +\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}d_j(x_j-x_{j+1})\\
&\le \sum_j\bar u_j\lambda_j^+
       +Lh\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}g_j,
\end{aligned}
\]
using respectively \(x_j\le\bar u_j\), \(x_j\ge0\),
\(x_{j+1}-x_j\le Lh\), and \(x_{j+1}-x_j\ge0\).  This is weak duality;
the multipliers constructed at \(x^*\) attain equality, proving the displayed
minimum formula.

The same equations are node-balance equations on the path
\(0,1,\ldots,m\): \(g_j\) and \(d_j\) are the two oriented arc flows, while
\(\lambda_j^+\) and \(\lambda_j^-\) are nonnegative node transactions.
The only nonzero arc capacity cost is \(Lh\sum_jg_j\), and the upper-obstacle
transactions cost \(\sum_j\bar u_j\lambda_j^+\).  A feasible primal vector
and feasible dual flow with the common displayed objective are therefore a
finite, directly checkable min-cost-transshipment certificate.

statements.statement: For every mesh \(h=1/m\), \(\mathcal T_h(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) and \(d_H^{\|\cdot\|_\infty}(\mathcal T_h(P_{\mathrm{obs}}),\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}}))\le2(Lh+Mh^\beta)\). The bound is uniform over \(P\in\mathfrak P\), including laws for which \(u_{a,z}\) has intervals or isolated points of zeros.
statements.justification: Two-sided Hausdorff control converts a numerical grid into a certified approximation to the entire sharp set.
statements.gap: Chiang et al. control sieve approximation inside confidence inequalities, but do not prove two-sided sup-norm Hausdorff approximation for a changing obstacle capacity.
statements.consumer: An analyst can choose \(h\) to guarantee that computational error is smaller than a prespecified clinical effect margin.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(\delta_h=Mh^\beta\).  We first verify the inner inclusion one
arm-profile pair at a time.  Let \(\Phi_hx\in\mathcal S^h_{a,z}\).  On each
interval \([r_j,r_{j+1}]\), its slope is
\((x_{j+1}-x_j)/h\in[0,L]\).  Hence \(\Phi_hx\) is nonnegative,
nondecreasing, and \(L\)-Lipschitz.  If
\(r\in[r_j,r_{j+1}]\) and \(k\in\{j,j+1\}\), the H\"older condition on
\(u_{a,z}\) gives
\[
 u_{a,z}(r)\ge u_{a,z}(r_k)-M|r-r_k|^\beta
             \ge u_{a,z}(r_k)-\delta_h.
\]
Because \(u_{a,z}(r)\ge0\), this implies
\[
 x_k\le [u_{a,z}(r_k)-\delta_h]_+\le u_{a,z}(r).
\]
The interpolant is a convex combination of \(x_j\) and \(x_{j+1}\), so
\(\Phi_hx(r)\le u_{a,z}(r)\).  All defining obstacle inequalities therefore
hold, proving
\(\mathcal S^h_{a,z}\subseteq\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).
Taking the finite product over \((a,z)\) and then applying the affine map in
the definition of the curve sets proves
\[
 \mathcal T_h(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]

For the reverse approximation, fix
\(f\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) and define the nodal vector
\[
 x_j=[f(r_j)-\delta_h]_+,
 \qquad j=0,\ldots,m.
\]
Since \(f(r_j)\le u_{a,z}(r_j)\),
\(x_j\le[u_{a,z}(r_j)-\delta_h]_+\).  The map
\(q(t)=[t-\delta_h]_+\) is nondecreasing and one-Lipschitz.  The monotonicity
and Lipschitz restrictions on \(f\) therefore imply
\[
 0\le x_{j+1}-x_j
 \le f(r_{j+1})-f(r_j)
 \le Lh.
\]
Thus \(\Phi_hx\in\mathcal S^h_{a,z}\).  Moreover,
\(|f(r_j)-x_j|\le\delta_h\) at every node.  Writing
\(r=(1-t)r_j+tr_{j+1}\), \(0\le t\le1\), and using the
\(L\)-Lipschitz property twice gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|f(r)-\{(1-t)f(r_j)+tf(r_{j+1})\}\right|
&\le(1-t)Lth+tL(1-t)h\\
&=2t(1-t)Lh\le Lh.
\end{aligned}
\]
The nodal clipping contributes at most \(\delta_h\), whence
\[
 \|f-\Phi_hx\|_\infty\le Lh+Mh^\beta.
\]

Now take any
\(g=(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z})_z\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).
Apply the preceding construction separately to every \(f_{a,z}\), obtaining
\(f^h_{a,z}\in\mathcal S^h_{a,z}\), and define
\(g^h=(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f^h_{1,z}-f^h_{0,z})_z\).  Then
\(g^h\in\mathcal T_h(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g-g^h\|_\infty
&\le\max_z\left(
 \|f_{1,z}-f^h_{1,z}\|_\infty+
 \|f_{0,z}-f^h_{0,z}\|_\infty\right)\\
&\le2(Lh+Mh^\beta).
\end{aligned}
\]
The inner inclusion makes the directed distance from
\(\mathcal T_h(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) to \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\)
zero, and the last display bounds the opposite directed distance.  Their
maximum is the asserted Hausdorff bound.  Every inequality used only the
common constants \(L,M,\beta\), so the bound is uniform over
\(P\in\mathfrak P\).  The proof never divides by \(u_{a,z}\) and the clipping
map is valid when its argument is zero; hence intervals and isolated points
on which \(u_{a,z}=0\) require no separate positivity condition.

statements.statement: For every \(g\in\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the constructed law \(P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), preserves the observed law, and satisfies \(\tau^{P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}}=g\). In particular, \(f^g_{1,z}=[g_z-b_{1,z}+b_{0,z}]_+\) and \(f^g_{0,z}=[-g_z+b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}]_+\) are continuous, obey \(0\le f^g_{a,z}\le u_{a,z}\), and the ratio completion is legal on both \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\) and \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\).
statements.justification: This separate attainability result prevents the residual-continuity benchmark from borrowing membership in the monotone-Lipschitz law class.
statements.gap: Wang et al. establish validity of covariatewise endpoints but do not construct a single residual-continuous full-data law for every curve in the continuous endpoint image.
statements.consumer: It certifies the exact benchmark against which the contraction produced by the clinically calibrated shape restrictions is measured.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(g\in\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) and put
\[
d_z(r):=g_z(r)-b_{1,z}(r)+b_{0,z}(r).
\]
The pointwise-image definition is equivalent to
\[
-u_{0,z}(r)\leq d_z(r)\leq u_{1,z}(r)\qquad(z\in\mathcal Z,\ r\in[0,1]). \qquad\text{(1)}
\]
The proposed residuals are the positive and negative parts
\[
f^g_{1,z}=d_z^+,
\qquad f^g_{0,z}=(-d_z)^+.
\]
Because \(g_z,b_{1,z},b_{0,z}\) are continuous and the positive-part map is continuous, both residuals are continuous.  From (1), considering separately \(d_z\geq0\) and \(d_z<0\),
\[
0\leq f^g_{1,z}(r)\leq u_{1,z}(r),
\qquad
0\leq f^g_{0,z}(r)\leq u_{0,z}(r).                                    \qquad\text{(2)}
\]
Also,
\[
f^g_{1,z}(r)-f^g_{0,z}(r)=d_z(r).                                      \qquad\text{(3)}
\]

Equation (2) shows that \(q^g_{a,z}=f^g_{a,z}/u_{a,z}\) is a probability on \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\).  On \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\), (2) forces \(f^g_{a,z}=0\), so the stipulated value \(q^g_{a,z}=0\) is legal and, on both regions,
\[
q^g_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)=f^g_{a,z}(r).                                   \qquad\text{(4)}
\]

We verify the induced observation rather than assuming it.  For an armwise sampled record \((\widetilde T_a,\Delta_a)\), if \(\Delta_a=0\), then \(T(a)=\widetilde T_a<C(a)=t_{\max}+1\); if \(\Delta_a=1\), then \(C(a)=\widetilde T_a\leq T(a)\).  Therefore in either case
\[
\min\{T(a),C(a)\}=\widetilde T_a,
\qquad \mathbf 1\{C(a)\leq T(a)\}=\Delta_a.                          \qquad\text{(5)}
\]
Together with the observed marginal of \(X\), the observed conditional arm kernels, and the protocol treatment probabilities, (5) proves that the observed law under \(P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  The construction draws treatment independently of both potential arm records given \(X\), gives consistency after setting \((T,C)=(T(A),C(A))\), and keeps \(T(a)\) in \([0,t_{\max}]\).

The same conditional calculation, now using (4), yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
s^{P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}}_{a,z}(r)
&=E[(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&=q^g_{a,z}(r)
E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta
 \mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&=q^g_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)
=f^g_{a,z}(r).                                                         \qquad\text{(6)}
\end{aligned}
\]
These residuals are continuous by (2), and no monotonicity or finite Lipschitz condition is required in the residual-continuity-only class.  All remaining overlap and observed-law regularity properties are inherited from \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Hence \(P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).

Finally, randomization, consistency, and the armwise decomposition of event time give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_z^{P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}}(r)
&=b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)
 +f^g_{1,z}(r)-f^g_{0,z}(r)\\
&=b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+d_z(r)
=g_z(r),                                                               \qquad\text{(7)}
\end{aligned}
\]
where (3) gives the second equality.  Thus one law attains the entire curve \(g\), including every zero-capacity contact.

statements.statement: For the separately defined residual-continuity-only compatible-law class, \(\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}=\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subset\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\). Its coordinate interval is \([b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-u_{0,z}(r),b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+u_{1,z}(r)]\), the continuous-curve image of the conservative endpoint formula in Wang et al., Theorem 5.1 and equations (8)--(9). For the maintained monotone-Lipschitz class, \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). A sufficient observed criterion for strict inclusion is the existence of \(z,r_1<r_2\) such that \(u_{1,z}(r_1)+u_{0,z}(r_2)>2L(r_2-r_1)\), because the two endpoint choices permitted by \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) violate the \(2L\)-Lipschitz restriction on \(f_{1,z}-f_{0,z}\).
statements.justification: The result gives a valid continuous-function sanity reduction and an observable sufficient certificate that curve coupling strictly improves on pointwise bounds.
statements.gap: Wang et al.'s endpoint theorem permits independent adversarial completions at each score value and supplies no observed sufficient criterion certifying that joint residual shape strictly contracts its product region.
statements.consumer: The sufficient condition identifies profiles and score pairs for which defending the residual-shape sensitivity model can change a treatment-benefit conclusion.
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
\Theta_{I,\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
:=\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For \(P\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the consistency identity and bounded-event-time inequality give
\[
0\leq s^P_{a,z}(r)\leq u_{a,z}(r)
\tag{2}
\]
for the conditional score law almost every \(r\).  Both functions are continuous in this class.  Profile mass, Bayes' rule, treatment overlap, and the density bound give
\[
\frac{dP_{\mathrm{obs}}(R\in dr\mid A=a,Z=z)}{dr}
=\frac{\pi_a(z,r)p_z(r)}
{P_{\mathrm{obs}}(A=a\mid Z=z)}
\geq\varepsilon c_p>0.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus (2) holds everywhere.  Conditional randomization and consistency give
\[
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-u_{0,z}(r)
\leq\tau_z^P(r)\leq
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+u_{1,z}(r).
\tag{4}
\]
The curve is continuous because the bases are H\"older and the residuals are continuous, so
\[
\Theta_{I,\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\subseteq\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{5}
\]
The established continuous-box completion lemma attains every \(g\in\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) by one \(P^g_{\mathrm{cont}}\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), proving
\[
\Theta_{I,\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{6}
\]
The continuous upper and lower endpoint curves belong to the box, and their convex mixtures fill every coordinate interval in (4).

The definitions also give
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_{a,z}(r)+u_{a,z}(r)
&=E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}
[\widetilde T+(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta
\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\\
&=E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}
[\widetilde T\mathbf 1\{\Delta=0\}
+t_{\max}\mathbf 1\{\Delta=1\}
\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r].
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
The cited Wang endpoint lemma identifies \(b_{a,z}\) as the lower arm endpoint, (7) as the upper arm endpoint, and forms CATE endpoints by subtracting opposite arm endpoints.  These differences are
\[
b_{1,z}-(b_{0,z}+u_{0,z})=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}-u_{0,z},
\qquad
(b_{1,z}+u_{1,z})-b_{0,z}=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+u_{1,z}.
\tag{8}
\]

For every \(g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), its residual difference is \(f_{1,z}-f_{0,z}\) with \(0\leq f_{a,z}\leq u_{a,z}\).  Hence
\[
\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{9}
\]
Suppose \(r_1<r_2\) and
\[
u_{1,z}(r_1)+u_{0,z}(r_2)>2L(r_2-r_1).
\tag{10}
\]
Let \(\lambda\) be zero on \([0,r_1]\), linear from zero to one on \([r_1,r_2]\), and one on \([r_2,1]\), and define
\[
d_z(r)=\{1-\lambda(r)\}u_{1,z}(r)-\lambda(r)u_{0,z}(r).
\tag{11}
\]
Set the other profile residual differences to zero and add them to the base curves.  Equation (11) is a pointwise convex combination of \(u_{1,z}\) and \(-u_{0,z}\), so this continuous curve lies in \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  But
\[
d_z(r_1)=u_{1,z}(r_1),\qquad
d_z(r_2)=-u_{0,z}(r_2),
\]
and (10) implies
\[
|d_z(r_2)-d_z(r_1)|>2L(r_2-r_1).
\tag{12}
\]
If the curve belonged to \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), then \(d_z=f_{1,z}-f_{0,z}\) for two \(L\)-Lipschitz functions, giving
\[
|d_z(r_2)-d_z(r_1)|
\leq|f_{1,z}(r_2)-f_{1,z}(r_1)|
+|f_{0,z}(r_2)-f_{0,z}(r_1)|
\leq2L(r_2-r_1),
\]
contrary to (12).  This proves the stated sufficient certificate.

statements.statement: For nonempty compact convex \(K_1,K_2\subset\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z,h_n}\) contained in the closed radius-\(\mathsf R\) ball, \(d_H(K_1,K_2)\le\max_{v\in\mathcal D_n}|h_{K_1}(v)-h_{K_2}(v)|+2\mathsf R\delta_n\).
statements.justification: The finite-net inequality converts support calibration on finitely many directions into Hausdorff control with an explicit geometric remainder.
statements.gap: Generic support-function identities take a supremum over the full dual ball; the gridded finite-dimensional reduction records the exact net remainder needed for the changing-contact rate.
statements.consumer: It makes the empirical-process prerequisite finite in the direction coordinate and exposes its \(\log|\mathcal D_n|\) cost.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(E=\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z,h_n}\) with its inherited norm, and write
\(B_E=\{x\in E:\|x\|\le1\}\).  We first establish directly the support
representation of Hausdorff distance needed here.  If
\(d=d_H(K_1,K_2)\), then
\(K_1\subseteq K_2+dB_E\) and \(K_2\subseteq K_1+dB_E\).  Therefore, for
every \(v\in E^*\),
\[
 |h_{K_1}(v)-h_{K_2}(v)|\le d\|v\|_*.
\]
Conversely, put
\[
 q=\sup_{\|v\|_*\le1}|h_{K_1}(v)-h_{K_2}(v)|.
\]
If some \(x\in K_1\) were outside the closed convex set \(K_2+qB_E\),
finite-dimensional separation would give a nonzero \(v\in E^*\) such that
\[
 v(x)>h_{K_2+qB_E}(v)=h_{K_2}(v)+q\|v\|_*.
\]
After division by \(\|v\|_*\), this contradicts the definition of \(q\).
Thus \(K_1\subseteq K_2+qB_E\); interchanging the sets gives the reverse
inclusion.  It follows that
\[
 d_H(K_1,K_2)=
 \sup_{\|v\|_*\le1}|h_{K_1}(v)-h_{K_2}(v)|.
\]

For any set \(K\) contained in the closed radius-\(\mathsf R\) ball and any
\(v,d\in E^*\),
\[
 |h_K(v)-h_K(d)|
 \le\sup_{x\in K}|(v-d)(x)|
 \le\mathsf R\|v-d\|_*.
\]
Given \(v\) in the dual unit ball, the definition of the
\(\delta_n\)-net supplies \(d\in\mathcal D_n\) with
\(\|v-d\|_*\le\delta_n\).  Applying the preceding Lipschitz bound to both
sets yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
|h_{K_1}(v)-h_{K_2}(v)|
&\le |h_{K_1}(d)-h_{K_2}(d)|
   +|h_{K_1}(v)-h_{K_1}(d)|
   +|h_{K_2}(v)-h_{K_2}(d)|\\
&\le \max_{e\in\mathcal D_n}|h_{K_1}(e)-h_{K_2}(e)|
   +2\mathsf R\delta_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over the dual unit ball and using the established
support representation proves the claim.

statements.statement: The band-robust theorem already gives contact-stable whole-set coverage and conservative simultaneous leaf projections. The remaining question is whether, uniformly over the externally certified subclass and through changing zero-capacity contacts and optimal faces, one can derive an explicit score-to-statistic expansion for gridded support values, baseline-law constraints, and optimized leaf endpoints, prove a controlled uniform remainder and conditional multiplier approximation, and calibrate one common multiplier critical value over the finite direction-net-by-leaf index set. The target is the sharper local-mass leaf-endpoint excess \(O_P(r_n/p_{\min,n}+\mathsf R\delta_n+\sqrt{(V_c\log n+\log|\mathcal D_n|+\log(1/\alpha))/(np_{\min,n})})\), with arbitrary post-selection validity inherited from the simultaneous event. No whole-set coverage claim remains open.
statements.justification: The direct stability theorem closes changing-contact whole-set coverage. What remains is the efficient score expansion, conditional multiplier coupling, and local-mass leaf calibration, none of which follows from envelope, moment, and entropy bounds alone.
statements.gap: Existing directional-delta and support-boundary methods do not supply the score-to-statistic expansion for this nuisance-dependent obstacle and its optimized leaf projections. The robust theorem bypasses that gap for whole-set coverage, but not for the sharper local-mass multiplier rate.
statements.consumer: Solving the residual question would sharpen the conservative simultaneous genomic-leaf intervals to the desired local-mass rate while preserving post-selection validity.

obligation.what_is_open: The missing step is a band-subclass-uniform asymptotic linearization that links the declared score class to the gridded support values, baseline-law constraints, and optimized leaf endpoints through changing optimal faces, followed by conditional validity of the one-common-multiplier critical value for that linked process.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen score assumptions impose only centering, an envelope moment bound, and an entropy bound. They define neither the statistics represented by the scores nor a uniform remainder or multiplier coupling. The admissible zero-score class satisfies every stated score condition but has multiplier critical value zero and cannot control a nondegenerate eligible-leaf mass error; thus the desired multiplier/leaf conclusion is not derivable from the declared primitives.
obligation.attempted: I derived a contact-set-uniform contraction of each obstacle by positive-part shifting and used it with the external nuisance band and the grid theorem. This closes the robust whole-set geometry without differentiating active faces. I then attempted to calibrate the baseline-law and leaf projections from the stated score process, but there is no declared score-to-statistic equation to which the moment and entropy controls can be applied; the zero-score witness confirms that this is not recoverable by empirical-process algebra alone.
obligation.partial_result:
The changing-contact geometry itself admits the following uniform bound.
For two nonnegative capacities \(u,u'\), set
\(\rho=\|u-u'\|_\infty\).  If \(f\in\mathcal S(u)\), define
\(C_\rho f=(f-\rho)_+\).  The positive-part map is nondecreasing and
one-Lipschitz, so \(C_\rho f\) remains nonnegative, nondecreasing, and
\(L\)-Lipschitz.  Since \(f\le u\le u'+\rho\), one also has
\(C_\rho f\le u'\), and
\(\|f-C_\rho f\|_\infty\le\rho\).  Interchanging \(u,u'\) proves
\[
 d_H\{\mathcal S(u),\mathcal S(u')\}\le\|u-u'\|_\infty,
\]
with no condition on either zero-capacity contact set.  Consequently, if
\(\rho_b=\max_{a,z}\|b_{a,z}-b'_{a,z}\|_\infty\) and
\(\rho_u=\max_{a,z}\|u_{a,z}-u'_{a,z}\|_\infty\), applying
\(C_{\rho_u}\) separately in the two arms gives
\[
 d_H\{\mathcal T(b,u),\mathcal T(b',u')\}
 \le2\rho_b+2\rho_u.
\]
On the event in the external-band prerequisite, every admissible nuisance
element in the band is within \(2r_n\) of the true nuisance.  Hence the
closure of the union of its admissible obstacle images is within
\(8r_n\) of the true curve set.  Expanding each gridded image by
\(2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), as justified by the grid theorem, gives an observable
robust-band whole-set superset that contains the true curve set on that event
and whose directed excess is at most
\(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), before any optional direction-net remainder.
Thus changing and even newly appearing contact sets do not obstruct the
whole-set rate.

What remains unproved is the simultaneous multiplier and leaf projection
part.  The current premises bound only the envelope, moment, and covering
numbers of \(\Psi_n\); no declared equation connects an element of
\(\Psi_n\) to the estimation error of a support value, a leaf numerator, a
leaf mass, or an endpoint optimizer, and no premise asserts a uniform
linearization remainder or conditional multiplier coupling.  This is a
logical, not merely technical, omission.  For example, take the score class
to consist of the zero function for every index in
\(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\).  It is centered, has zero envelope
moment, and has covering number one, so all three stated score conditions
hold.  Nevertheless, for an eligible leaf \(G\) with \(P_X(G)=1/2\) and an
odd sample size \(n\), the empirical leaf mass cannot equal \(1/2\), whereas
the multiplier supremum of the zero score class and its critical value are
identically zero.  Hence the declared score conditions alone do not control
even the leaf-mass error, much less the optimized leaf endpoints.  A complete
positive theorem must first define the support and leaf statistics and prove
a band-subclass-uniform score expansion for them, including the optimizer's
changing critical cone, and must then establish conditional multiplier
quantile validity for that expansion.  Neither required link is a consequence
of the frozen premises.

statements.statement: Under the causal conditions of Wang et al., their conservative post-dropout formula has arm-specific lower endpoint \(E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[\widetilde T\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\) and upper endpoint \(E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}[\widetilde T\mathbf 1\{\Delta=0\}+t_{\max}\mathbf 1\{\Delta=1\}\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]\); the CATE lower endpoint subtracts the control-arm upper endpoint from the treated-arm lower endpoint, and the CATE upper endpoint subtracts the control-arm lower endpoint from the treated-arm upper endpoint.

source.locator: Equation (4), equation (8), and Theorem 5.1 with equation (9) in arXiv:2510.13397v3, pages 5--6 of the PDF

attestation.note: Transcribed from the displayed formulas at the cited locations in version 3 of the source PDF.

statements.statement:
Fix an arm and profile.  If the obstacle-set construction is evaluated at two nonnegative continuous capacities \(u_{a,z}\) and \(u'_{a,z}\), then
\[
d_H^{\|\cdot\|_\infty}\!\left(\mathcal S_{a,z}(u),\mathcal S_{a,z}(u')\right)
\leq \|u_{a,z}-u'_{a,z}\|_\infty.
\]
Consequently, for two base-capacity pairs \((b,u)\) and \((b',u')\), with
\[
\rho_b=\max_{a,z}\|b_{a,z}-b'_{a,z}\|_\infty,
\qquad
\rho_u=\max_{a,z}\|u_{a,z}-u'_{a,z}\|_\infty,
\]
the corresponding sharp-curve constructions obey
\[
d_H^{\|\cdot\|_\infty}\!\left(\mathcal T(b,u),\mathcal T(b',u')\right)
\leq 2\rho_b+2\rho_u.
\]
Both inequalities hold without any restriction on the zero-capacity contact sets.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\rho=\|u_{a,z}-u'_{a,z}\|_\infty\), and fix \(f\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(u)\).  Define
\[
(C_\rho f)(r):=[f(r)-\rho]_+.
\tag{1}
\]
The map \(x\mapsto[x-\rho]_+\) is nondecreasing and one-Lipschitz.  Since \(f\) is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and \(L\)-Lipschitz by the obstacle-set definition, (1) is also nonnegative and nondecreasing and satisfies
\[
|(C_\rho f)(r)-(C_\rho f)(r')|
\leq |f(r)-f(r')|
\leq L|r-r'|.
\tag{2}
\]
Moreover, \(f\leq u_{a,z}\leq u'_{a,z}+\rho\) and \(u'_{a,z}\geq0\), whence
\[
0\leq C_\rho f\leq u'_{a,z}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(C_\rho f\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(u')\).  Pointwise,
\[
0\leq f(r)-[f(r)-\rho]_+=\min\{f(r),\rho\}\leq\rho,
\tag{4}
\]
so every element of \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(u)\) is within \(\rho\) of \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(u')\).  Interchanging \(u_{a,z}\) and \(u'_{a,z}\) proves the first Hausdorff inequality.  Notice that (1)--(4) remain valid when either capacity vanishes on an interval or at an isolated point.

For the curve claim, fix
\[
g_z=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+f_{1,z}-f_{0,z}\in\mathcal T(b,u).
\]
Apply (1) armwise with \(\rho_u\), writing \(f'_{a,z}=C_{\rho_u}f_{a,z}\).  Then \(f'_{a,z}\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(u')\), and
\[
g'_z=b'_{1,z}-b'_{0,z}+f'_{1,z}-f'_{0,z}\in\mathcal T(b',u').
\]
The triangle inequality and (4) give
\[
\|g-g'\|_\infty
\leq \max_z\bigl(\|b_{1,z}-b'_{1,z}\|_\infty
+\|b_{0,z}-b'_{0,z}\|_\infty
+\|f_{1,z}-f'_{1,z}\|_\infty
+\|f_{0,z}-f'_{0,z}\|_\infty\bigr)
\leq2\rho_b+2\rho_u.
\tag{5}
\]
The same construction with the primed and unprimed pairs exchanged gives the reverse directed bound, proving the second Hausdorff inequality.
statements.justification: This contraction argument is the contact-uniform modulus needed to propagate an external nuisance band through the obstacle image.
statements.gap: Directional differentiation can change discontinuously when zero-capacity contacts appear, but the positive-part contraction controls the entire feasible set without differentiating a face.
statements.consumer: It supplies the deterministic \(8r_n\) robust-union excess term in the band-robust confidence theorem.

statements.statement:
For every nonnegative continuous capacity \(u_{a,z}\), the envelope \(\Gamma_Lu_{a,z}\) is the greatest element of \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\): it is nonnegative, nondecreasing, \(L\)-Lipschitz, bounded above by \(u_{a,z}\), and every \(f\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) satisfies
\[
f(r)\leq(\Gamma_Lu_{a,z})(r)\qquad\text{for every }r\in[0,1].
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(a,z\), abbreviate \(u=u_{a,z}\), and put
\[
G(r):=(\Gamma_Lu)(r)=\inf_{t\in[0,1]}\{u(t)+L(r-t)_+\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Every term under the infimum is nonnegative, so \(G\geq0\).  Taking \(t=r\) gives
\[
G(r)\leq u(r).
\tag{2}
\]
If \(r\leq r'\), then \((r-t)_+\leq(r'-t)_+\) for every \(t\), hence \(G(r)\leq G(r')\).  Also
\[
0\leq(r'-t)_+-(r-t)_+\leq r'-r.
\tag{3}
\]
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(t_\varepsilon\) whose value in (1) is at most \(G(r)+\varepsilon\).  Then
\[
G(r')
\leq u(t_\varepsilon)+L(r'-t_\varepsilon)_+
\leq G(r)+\varepsilon+L(r'-r).
\]
Letting \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), and combining this inequality with monotonicity, proves
\[
0\leq G(r')-G(r)\leq L(r'-r).
\tag{4}
\]
Thus \(G\) is nonnegative, nondecreasing, \(L\)-Lipschitz, and below \(u\), so \(G\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).

Let \(f\in\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  For fixed \(r,t\), if \(t\leq r\), the Lipschitz restriction and \(f(t)\leq u(t)\) give
\[
f(r)\leq f(t)+L(r-t)\leq u(t)+L(r-t)_+.
\]
If \(t>r\), monotonicity and the obstacle inequality give
\[
f(r)\leq f(t)\leq u(t)=u(t)+L(r-t)_+.
\]
Taking the infimum over \(t\) proves \(f(r)\leq G(r)\).  Since \(r\) was arbitrary, \(G\) is the greatest obstacle element.
statements.justification: The explicit envelope converts the obstacle constraint into a computable greatest feasible residual and is the key to exact pointwise projection.
statements.gap: The obstacle definition alone does not expose its greatest element or show that the pointwise residual maximum can be attained by one globally feasible function.
statements.consumer: The exact pointwise projection theorem uses this lemma for both arm endpoints.

statements.statement:
For every \(z\in\mathcal Z\) and \(r\in[0,1]\), the exact coordinate projection is
\[
\{g_z(r):g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
=\left[
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-(\Gamma_Lu_{0,z})(r),
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+(\Gamma_Lu_{1,z})(r)
\right].
\]
Thus the displayed interval is sharp, not merely outer.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(z,r\) and write \(c_z=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}\).  If \(g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), then
\[
g_z(r)=c_z(r)+f_{1,z}(r)-f_{0,z}(r)
\tag{1}
\]
for obstacle functions \(f_{a,z}\).  The greatest-obstacle lemma and nonnegativity give
\[
0\leq f_{a,z}(r)\leq(\Gamma_Lu_{a,z})(r).
\tag{2}
\]
Equations (1)--(2) prove the outer inclusion in the displayed interval.

Conversely, the zero function is feasible, and the greatest-obstacle lemma makes \(\Gamma_Lu_{a,z}\) feasible.  The lower endpoint is attained by \(f_{0,z}=\Gamma_Lu_{0,z}\), \(f_{1,z}=0\); the upper endpoint is attained by \(f_{1,z}=\Gamma_Lu_{1,z}\), \(f_{0,z}=0\).  Set unused arm-profile functions to zero.  Every defining obstacle inequality is preserved by convex combinations, so convex mixtures of these two feasible families attain every scalar between the endpoints.  This proves equality.
statements.justification: This theorem gives the exact scalar projection of the joint curve set while preserving the distinction between a projection and the whole identified set.
statements.gap: Pointwise capacity endpoints ignore monotone-Lipschitz feasibility; the greatest-obstacle envelope supplies the attainable corrected endpoints.
statements.consumer: Analysts can read exact scorewise sign bounds from the jointly sharp curve set.

statements.statement:
For the nonnegative continuous capacities in the frozen setup,
\[
\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subsetneq\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\max_{a\in\mathcal A,\,z\in\mathcal Z}\|u_{a,z}\|_\infty>0.
\]
If the maximum is zero, both sets are the singleton base curve.  If it is positive, a continuous box selection has local slope exceeding \(L\), whereas every residual difference generated by two monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz obstacles is itself \(L\)-Lipschitz.
statements.proof_tex:
Every \(g\in\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) has
\[
g_z=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+d_z,\qquad
d_z=f_{1,z}-f_{0,z},\qquad
0\leq f_{a,z}\leq u_{a,z}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(-u_{0,z}\leq d_z\leq u_{1,z}\), proving
\[
\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{2}
\]
For \(r<r'\), obstacle monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity imply
\[
0\leq f_{a,z}(r')-f_{a,z}(r)\leq L(r'-r),\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{3}
\]
The difference of the two increments in (3) lies in \([-L(r'-r),L(r'-r)]\), whence
\[
|d_z(r')-d_z(r)|\leq L|r'-r|.
\tag{4}
\]

Suppose the maximum capacity norm is positive.  Nonnegativity yields \(a_0,z_0,r_0\) with \(u_{a_0,z_0}(r_0)>0\).  Continuity supplies \(c>0\) and a nondegenerate relative interval \(J\subset[0,1]\) on which \(u_{a_0,z_0}\geq c\).  Choose \(x<y<w\) in the relative interior of \(J\) so that
\[
y-x<\frac{c}{2L}.
\tag{5}
\]
Let \(\psi\) be a continuous triangular tent supported on \([x,w]\), linear from \(\psi(x)=0\) to \(\psi(y)=c/2\), linear back to \(\psi(w)=0\), and zero elsewhere.  Then
\[
0\leq\psi\leq u_{a_0,z_0}.
\tag{6}
\]
Define
\[
d_{z_0}=
\begin{cases}
\psi,&a_0=1,\\
-\psi,&a_0=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
d_z=0\ (z\neq z_0),\qquad
g_z=b_{1,z}-b_{0,z}+d_z.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) imply \(-u_{0,z}\leq d_z\leq u_{1,z}\), so \(g\in\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  But
\[
|d_{z_0}(y)-d_{z_0}(x)|=\frac c2>L(y-x),
\tag{8}
\]
contradicting (4) for every member of \(\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Inclusion (2) is therefore strict.

Conversely, if every capacity norm is zero, nonnegativity gives \(u_{a,z}=0\) for every arm and profile.  The obstacle and box inequalities then force every residual to be zero, so
\[
\mathcal T(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
=\{(b_{1,z}-b_{0,z})_{z\in\mathcal Z}\}.
\]
This proves the equivalence.
statements.justification: The equivalence is the exact observable frontier for whether scorewise shape restrictions contract the continuous Wang endpoint box.
statements.gap: The former score-pair condition was only sufficient and used a loose two-(L) difference bound; monotone arm increments sharpen the residual difference to one-(L) Lipschitz continuity.
statements.consumer: It determines exactly when the maintained curve set adds identifying content beyond continuous endpoint selection.

statements.statement:
For every measurable endpoint selection \(g\in\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), there is one full-data law \(P^g\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) such that
\[
\tau^{P^g}=g\qquad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
The completion preserves the entire observed law and remains legal on every zero-capacity contact set.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(g\in\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and choose a jointly measurable representative \(\bar g\) of this element of \(L^0(P_X)\).  Write
\[
c_z(r)=b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r).
\]
By the definition of \(\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the measurable set
\[
N=\{(z,r):\bar g_z(r)<c_z(r)-u_{0,z}(r)\text{ or }\bar g_z(r)>c_z(r)+u_{1,z}(r)\}
\]
has \(P_X(N)=0\).  Replace \(\bar g\) on \(N\) by \(c\), which does not change its \(L^0(P_X)\) equivalence class, and denote the resulting measurable representative again by \(g\).  Thus the box inequalities hold at every point for this representative.  Define
\[
f^g_{1,z}(r)=[g_z(r)-c_z(r)]_+,
\qquad
f^g_{0,z}(r)=[c_z(r)-g_z(r)]_+.
\tag{1}
\]
For every \((z,r)\), elementary positive-part algebra and the two box inequalities give
\[
0\le f^g_{a,z}(r)\le u_{a,z}(r),
\qquad
f^g_{1,z}(r)-f^g_{0,z}(r)=g_z(r)-c_z(r).
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, if \(u_{a,z}(r)=0\), then (2) forces \(f^g_{a,z}(r)=0\).  Hence the measurable function
\[
q^g_{a,z}(r)=
\begin{cases}
f^g_{a,z}(r)/u_{a,z}(r),&u_{a,z}(r)>0,\\
0,&u_{a,z}(r)=0
\end{cases}
\tag{3}
\]
is well defined and takes values in \([0,1]\); division is used only on the positive-capacity set.

We now use the armwise completion technique.  The identically zero family belongs to every obstacle set \(\mathcal S_{a,z}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\): it is continuous, nonnegative, nondecreasing, \(L\)-Lipschitz, and bounded above by the nonnegative capacity \(u_{a,z}\).  Therefore the established completion-witness lemma and the completion-law definition provide a law \(P^0\in\mathcal F(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Under that law, for each arm define
\[
\widetilde T_a^0=\min\{T^0(a),C^0(a)\},
\qquad
\Delta_a^0=\mathbf 1\{C^0(a)\le T^0(a)\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Conditional on \(X\), the law of \((\widetilde T_a^0,\Delta_a^0)\) is the observed conditional law of \((\widetilde T,\Delta)\) given \(A=a,X\).  Moreover, the zero-completion construction gives
\[
C^0(a)=t_{\max}+1,quad T^0(a)=\widetilde T_a^0
\quad\text{on }\{\Delta_a^0=0\},
\]
and
\[
C^0(a)=T^0(a)=\widetilde T_a^0
\quad\text{on }\{\Delta_a^0=1\}.
\tag{5}
\]

On a product extension of \(P^0\), draw \(U_0,U_1\) independently from the uniform law on \([0,1]\), independently of all variables under \(P^0\), and put
\[
T^g(a)=
\begin{cases}
t_{\max},&\Delta_a^0=1\text{ and }U_a\le q^g_{a,Z}(R),\\
\widetilde T_a^0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad
C^g(a)=C^0(a).
\tag{6}
\]
Finally, retain the baseline law and draw \(A\) conditionally on \(X\) with the protocol probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\), independently of the armwise potential vector and the uniforms; set \((T,C)=(T^g(A),C^g(A))\).  Call the resulting full-data law \(P^g\).

We first verify preservation of the observed law.  On \(\{\Delta_a^0=0\}\), equations (5)--(6) give \(T^g(a)=\widetilde T_a^0<C^g(a)=t_{\max}+1\), so the observed pair remains \((\widetilde T_a^0,0)\).  On \(\{\Delta_a^0=1\}\), one has \(C^g(a)=\widetilde T_a^0\) and either \(T^g(a)=\widetilde T_a^0\) or \(T^g(a)=t_{\max}\ge\widetilde T_a^0\).  The stipulated tie convention therefore gives the same observed pair \((\widetilde T_a^0,1)\).  Thus, arm by arm and conditional on \(X\),
\[
\left(\min\{T^g(a),C^g(a)\},
\mathbf 1\{C^g(a)\le T^g(a)\}\right)
=(\widetilde T_a^0,\Delta_a^0),
\tag{7}
\]
and the protocol treatment kernel then implies that the entire law of \((Z,R,A,\widetilde T,\Delta)\) under \(P^g\) is \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  Equations (5)--(6) and boundedness of the observed follow-up give \(0\le T^g(a)\le t_{\max}\).

The conditional randomization assumption for \(P^0\) makes \(A\) independent of its full armwise potential vector given \(X\).  Since the new uniforms are also conditionally independent of \(A\), (6) is a measurable armwise transformation and hence
\[
T^g(a)\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X.
\tag{8}
\]
Consistency holds by the assigned-arm definition of \((T,C)\), and treatment overlap is preserved because the kernel remains \(\pi_a(X)\).  Censoring overlap is preserved by (7).  The essential-overlap restriction supplies, for each arm, an observed conditional version bounded below by \(\kappa\) off a conditional-null set.  Treatment overlap makes the union of those exceptional sets \(P_X\)-null.  On that null union, redefine the conditional version to put probability one on an uncensored record.  Such a null-set redefinition leaves all defining conditional-integral identities, and hence \(P^g\), unchanged, while satisfying the pointwise overlap convention in the definition of \(\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Consequently, by that definition,
\[
P^g\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{9}
\]
No continuity, monotonicity, or Lipschitz property of \(f^g\) has been invoked in this membership argument.

It remains to compute the causal curve.  Conditional independence of \(U_a\), equations (3), (6), and observed-law preservation yield, for \(P_X\)-almost every \((z,r)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
&E_{P^g}\!\left[(T^g(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta
\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r\right]\\
&\qquad=q^g_{a,z}(r)
E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}\!\left[(t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta
\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r\right]\\
&\qquad=q^g_{a,z}(r)u_{a,z}(r)
=f^g_{a,z}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
The last equality follows by division on \(\{u_{a,z}>0\}\) and is \(0=0\) on \(\{u_{a,z}=0\}\), by (2).  On the assigned arm,
\[
T^g(a)=\widetilde T+(T^g(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta,
\]
so (8), the observed-base definition, and (10) give
\[
E_{P^g}[T^g(a)\mid Z=z,R=r]
=b_{a,z}(r)+f^g_{a,z}(r)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{11}
\]
Subtracting (11) for the two arms and using (1)--(2) and the CATE-curve definition proves
\[
\tau_z^{P^g}(r)
=c_z(r)+f^g_{1,z}(r)-f^g_{0,z}(r)
=g_z(r)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus one law attains the entire measurable selection simultaneously, including on all zero-capacity contact sets, and the claim follows.
statements.justification: The measurable extension of the armwise completion proves converse attainability for the full Wang-compatible image, including zero-capacity contacts.
statements.gap: The frozen continuous completion proves attainability only in the continuous slice and therefore cannot alone establish the full measurable image modulo null sets.
statements.consumer: The Wang-compatible box-sharpness theorem uses this completion for its reverse inclusion.

statements.statement:
For the Wang-compatible class,
\[
\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
=\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\text{in }L^0(P_X).
\]
The residual-continuity compatible class is a smaller witness subclass,
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\subseteq\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\]
and, under profile mass, score density, and observed-law continuity,
\[
\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\cap\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}
=\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]
Every member of this continuous slice is attained by a law in \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).
statements.proof_tex:
The observable map sends a full-data law \(P\) to the law of
\[
O=(Z,R,A,\min\{T(A),C(A)\},\mathbf 1\{C(A)\le T(A)\})
\in\mathcal Z\times[0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times[0,t_{\max}]\times\{0,1\}.
\]
For a fixed image \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the Wang identified set is
\[
\Theta_{I,W}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
:=\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
\subseteq L^0(P_X).
\]
This definition fixes the causal target; the endpoint box is a separate functional of the observed law.  We prove their equality by two inclusions and then identify the continuous slice.

First fix \(P\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), an arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and a covariate value \(x=(z,r)\) in a common full-\(P_X\)-measure set on which the relevant regular conditional expectations are defined.  Treatment exchangeability in the definition of the Wang-compatible class, together with treatment overlap, gives
\[
E_P[T(a)\mid X=x]
=E_P[T(a)\mid A=a,X=x].
\tag{1}
\]
Consistency and the definitions of \(\widetilde T\) and \(\Delta\) imply on \(\{A=a\}\) that
\[
T(a)=\widetilde T+(T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta.
\tag{2}
\]
Indeed, when \(\Delta=0\), one has \(C>T(a)\) and \(\widetilde T=T(a)\); when \(\Delta=1\), (2) is algebraic.  On the latter event, \(C\le T(a)\), hence \(\widetilde T=C\le T(a)\).  The bounded-event-time restriction therefore yields
\[
0\le (T(a)-\widetilde T)\Delta
\le (t_{\max}-\widetilde T)\Delta.
\tag{3}
\]
Taking conditional expectations in (2)--(3), using (1), using compatibility to replace the assigned-arm observed conditional law by \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and then applying the observed-base and dropout-capacity definitions gives
\[
b_{a,z}(r)
\le E_P[T(a)\mid Z=z,R=r]
\le b_{a,z}(r)+u_{a,z}(r)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{4}
\]
The cited Wang endpoint lemma confirms that the two expressions in (4) are exactly the published conservative lower and upper arm endpoints: its upper endpoint equals
\[
E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}
[\widetilde T\mathbf 1\{\Delta=0\}+t_{\max}\mathbf 1\{\Delta=1\}
\mid A=a,Z=z,R=r]
=b_{a,z}(r)+u_{a,z}(r).
\tag{5}
\]
By linearity of conditional expectation, the CATE definition, and (4), subtracting the control upper endpoint from the treatment lower endpoint and conversely gives
\[
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)-u_{0,z}(r)
\le\tau_z^P(r)\le
b_{1,z}(r)-b_{0,z}(r)+u_{1,z}(r)
\quad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus
\[
\{\tau^P:P\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}
\subseteq\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\quad\text{in }L^0(P_X).
\tag{7}
\]
Conversely, the measurable-box-completion lemma constructs, for every \(g\in\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), a single law \(P^g\in\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) satisfying \(\tau^{P^g}=g\) \(P_X\)-almost surely.  Therefore the reverse inclusion holds, and (7) is an equality.  This proves law sharpness, not merely an outer bound.

We next compare the continuous witness class.  If \(P\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), the continuity-model and compatibility definitions give consistency, bounded event-time support, treatment overlap, censoring overlap, and the same observed law.  Its conditional randomization restriction
\[
A\perp\!\!\!\perp(T(0),T(1),C(0),C(1))\mid X
\]
implies the weaker Wang restriction \(T(a)\perp\!\!\!\perp A\mid X\) for each arm.  Uniform essential censoring overlap permits a regular-conditional version bounded below by \(\kappa\) on a full-\(P_X\)-measure set; defining that version by any strictly positive uncensored kernel on the null complement gives the pointwise convention without changing the law.  The Wang class imposes no residual continuity, monotonicity, finite-Lipschitz, or independent-censoring restriction.  Hence every restriction defining the Wang-compatible class holds and
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\subseteq\mathcal F_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\tag{8}
\]

Finally, identify \(\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\) with its image in \(L^0(P_X)\).  This embedding is injective under profile mass and the score-density lower bound.  Indeed, if two continuous curve families differ at some \((z,r_0)\), continuity gives a nonempty relative interval \(I\subseteq[0,1]\) on which they differ, whereas
\[
P_X(Z=z,R\in I)
=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Z=z)\int_I p_z(t)\,dt
\ge\omega c_p\operatorname{Leb}(I)>0,
\tag{9}
\]
contradicting equality in \(L^0(P_X)\).

If \(g\in\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), its defining inequalities hold for every \((z,r)\), and hence almost surely; therefore
\[
\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
\subseteq\mathcal B_W(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\cap\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}.
\tag{10}
\]
For the reverse inclusion, let \(g\in\mathbb C_{\mathcal Z}\) satisfy the Wang box inequalities \(P_X\)-almost surely.
